recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Create a portrait-first browser game called Pastel Quest Contractor: a kawaii, satirical, Zelda-adjacent block builder where Mimi the cat contractor uses one-thumb mobile controls to place and clear pastel blocks around a looping temple pit. Preserve the original first-person 3D sandbox mechanics: left drag moves, right drag looks, right tap interacts, hotbar selects materials, inventory remaps slots, jump/fly buttons remain reachable, raycast placement/removal works within reach, collisions and terrain chunks remain grid-based, and the void loops the player back. Transform presentation through pastel dream UI, popcore fonts, meme feedback, snack/block material names, soft temple world language, and fast lunch-break onboarding.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Truth
- genre: Mobile-first first-person 3D sandbox block-builder with procedural chunks and an infinite central pit.
- objective: Move, look, place blocks, clear blocks, select materials, build across/around the generated terrain, and recover from the looping void.
- input model: Left touch zone controls movement, right touch zone controls camera look and tap-to-interact; hotbar selects block/tool; jump and fly buttons are touch-friendly; settings/inventory are modal buttons.
- core loop: Start run, generate terrain chunks, move camera/avatar, raycast at center crosshair, place or remove blocks within reach, collide against block geometry, update height/depth signal, loop player back after deep fall.
- fail/friction state: No hard loss; friction comes from blocked placement, out-of-range interaction, collision, gravity, and falling into the pit/void loop.

## Protected Mechanics
- Preserve first-person camera, reach-limited raycast placement/removal, block-grid terrain, hotbar and inventory assignment, collision body, jump/fly toggles, procedural chunk generation, pit omission, rim warning blocks, particle feedback, void loop reset, and touch zones.

## Remix Direction
Building-game mechanics are reframed as a satirical kawaii quest-contractor job: Mimi places pastel temple blocks during a lunch-break Zelda-adjacent zoning crisis. Presentation, HUD words, palette, material names, feedback, fonts, and background motifs are safe transformation surfaces; mechanics remain unchanged.
